documents.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can accelerate knowledge-work tasks, but task-level efficiency does not necessarily translate into shorter working hours or improved employee welfare. This article proposes an AI time-dividend allocation framework that separates the creation of saved time from its subsequent use. Drawing on the job demands–resources perspective, it examines a resource pathway through perceived time savings and work–life balance alongside a competing demand pathway through work intensification. The reported three-wave observational survey comprises 472 complete cases. Standardized ordinary least squares models with HC3 robust standard errors indicate that GenAI use intensity is associated with perceived time savings (β = .495, p < .001). Time savings is positively associated with work–life balance (β = .255, p < .001), whereas work intensification is negatively associated with work–life balance (β = −.443, p < .001). Reported bootstrap indirect effects are positive through time savings (0.126, 95% CI [0.079, 0.176]) and negative through time savings and work intensification (−0.036, 95% CI [−0.059, −0.015]). Performance pressure is positively associated with intensification, but its proposed interaction with time savings is not statistically significant. The findings are consistent with competing allocation pathways; given the observational design, they should not be interpreted as causal effects. The article identifies time-dividend allocation as a consequential dimension of AI-enabled work design.

Paper 1 of 2 in the AI Governance & Accountability Dossier. As AI shapes decisions about benefits, work, housing, credit, education and information, this paper asks who can inspect a system, challenge its use, and require a remedy. It reviews the 2025-26 U.S. governance landscape, including the GAO requirement count, OMB M-25-21 and M-25-22, Executive Order 14365 and state activity, and separates rules from remedies. It proposes a six-question diagnostic (authority, responsibility, evidence, visibility, challenge, remedy), a Minimum Accountability Package that works without a new office, and a comparison of three institutional models, including an elected state-level commissioner with independent technical staff. It treats the human-factors evidence as narrow, states what would change its conclusions, and labels every material claim in a ledger as documented, reported, interpretation or hypothesis. Not peer reviewed. Not legal advice. Research cut-off October 14, 2026.

documents.abstract: This study examines the effects of work environment, work supervision, and job training on occupational safety and health (K3) and work productivity, as well as the effect of K3 on work productivity among 200 employees at CV Griya Fajar Konstruksi, South Tangerang. A quantitative approach was employed using survey data from 200 employees and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). The results show that work environment and work supervision have positive and statistically significant effects on K3 and work productivity, while K3 has the strongest positive relationship with work productivity (β = 0.989; p < 0.001). In contrast, job training shows negative and statistically significant relationships with K3 (β = −0.437; p = 0.034) and work productivity (β = −0.285; p = 0.041). Five of the seven hypotheses are supported. The findings qualify the expected positive role of training by indicating that its provision alone does not necessarily translate into improved safety and productivity. The findings also highlight the importance of integrating supportive working conditions, consistent supervision, effective K3 practices, and relevant and practical training to support safe and productive construction operations.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: This study compared the image-based workplace safety judgments of three general-purpose AI assistants across five occupational contexts. Fifteen workplace images representing construction, workshop/manufacturing, maintenance/technical service, warehouse/logistics, and laboratory settings were evaluated by ChatGPT GPT-5.5, Claude Sonnet 5, and Gemini 3.5 Flash. Each model completed 15 single-image assessments and five within-context relative-ranking tasks, yielding 60 outputs. Two occupational safety specialists independently rated the outputs on five 0–5 dimensions and six binary error patterns. The raters showed exact or near-exact score agreement in 81.8% of the ordinal ratings; pooled quadratic weighted agreement was moderate, κ = 0.479, 95% CI [0.340, 0.595]. Agreement was complete for pairwise ranking accuracy and exact final ordering. Based on the two-rater means, ChatGPT led in visible evidence coverage (4.37), visual fidelity (4.43), prioritization (3.73), and uncertainty discipline (4.70), whereas Claude obtained the highest descriptive control-guidance mean (4.40). Between-model differences were statistically significant in the other four dimensions but not in control guidance. No rater-confirmed problematic control recommendation was observed. All three models achieved the same final-match performance: four of five context rankings were fully correct and 14 of 15 pairwise relations were correct. The shared failure occurred in the workshop/manufacturing context, where the image containing a visible person at height was ranked below a dusty but static scene. The findings support supervised first-pass use of AI assistants but not autonomous workplace safety evaluation.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: This study examines the relationships among intrinsic motivation, workplace thriving, and spirituality among teachers in Nigeria. The researchers collected data from 399 teachers and analysed the data using structural equation modelling with SmartPLS 3 and SPSS. The results showed that workplace spirituality was positively and strongly associated with workplace thriving, while intrinsic motivation was also significantly associated with workplace thriving. Further analysis showed that the work meaningfulness mediated the relationship between workplace spirituality and workplace thriving. In addition, the interaction between workplace spirituality and intrinsic motivation significantly influenced workplace thriving. The findings highlight the importance of workplace spirituality, intrinsic motivation, and work meaningfulness in promoting workplace thriving among secondary school teachers. Important practical implications are presented.

Series: A Plaine and Easie Introduction to Digital Music Scholarship (Workshop 2 of 5), The University of Melbourne, 27 August – 1 October 2026About this workshopIn this workshop we’ll take a look at an important archive of concert programs and memorabilia that document concert life in twentieth-century Melbourne, now part of the Rare Music Collection here at the University. It is a vast resource—over a hundred boxes covering not only orchestral, choral, and chamber concerts, but theater, ballet, jazz, too. To date, the only way into the collection is via a 300-page typescript summary. While this is a helpful guide, it hardly provides scholars and librarians with the control they need to explore the riches within. In this workshop, we will show how new digital tools (including Large Language Models) can help us extract structured data from the guide—and tell hidden stories about the people, spaces, and music of Melbourne’s past.With the assistance of Holden Starkey (Haverford College Class of 2027).Thursday 3 September 2026, Room 721, Building 880, The University of Melbourne.Slides: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1HSUVoYI0--jTYCSTDefQpxCtHZEGgctF6UxSdQPCMSk/edit Workshop page (data, code and other materials): https://sites.google.com/haverford.edu/melbourne2026workshops/hidden-history-melbourneAbout the seriesThis is one of a series of five workshops organized by Professor Richard Freedman (Haverford College, USA), in collaboration with Dr. Daniel Russo-Batterham (MDAP, Melbourne University) and Dr. Nick Tochka (Department of Music, Melbourne University). In them, we will explore the many ways in which the study of music and musical culture are being transformed by digital tools, from score to archive.These hands-on workshops are designed for anyone interested in learning more about digital approaches to the study of music. The focus here will be on ‘metadata’ (the who, what, when and where of musical artefacts), and how we model them in digital form. Using a few case studies as our focal points (including collections right here in Melbourne) participants will learn how we collect, organize, clean, analyze and interpret music metadata using various tools--especially Python and Pandas (a powerful library for data analysis). They will come away with a new understanding of how digital tools work. They will also learn to think critically about the ways in which information about music is organized, and the values implicit in the archives through which it is curated, discovered, and shared.

ABSTRACT Background Writing motivation and self‐efficacy are critical factors of success in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) contexts, yet they are frequently undermined by learner anxiety and limited teacher feedback. While artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots offer potential for adaptive writing support, limited research has examined these affective constructs in parallel across learner proficiency levels. Objectives This study investigated changes in intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, and writing self‐efficacy among high school EFL learners at higher‐ and lower‐proficiency levels following chatbot‐supported writing and examined whether these changes differed across proficiency levels. Methods Using an exploratory mixed‐methods design, the study involved 47 Vietnamese high school students divided into higher‐ and lower‐proficiency level groups. Over the 11‐week study, participants completed 8 weeks of AI‐supported writing activities using a chatbot designed in accordance with principles of Self‐Determination Theory, Self‐Regulated Learning Theory and Self‐Efficacy Theory. Changes in intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, and writing self‐efficacy were examined using pre‐ and post‐questionnaires and semi‐structured interviews. Results and Conclusions The quantitative findings revealed that intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, and writing self‐efficacy increased over time in both proficiency groups, with no significant differences in the magnitude of change between higher‐ and lower‐proficiency learners. This suggests that the affective changes observed during AI‐supported writing were not confined to one proficiency group. The qualitative findings indicated that learners linked their positive experiences to reduced anxiety, clearer guidance, and supportive interaction, although the types of support they valued differed by proficiency level. Overall, the findings suggest that when positioned as a supportive writing partner rather than an answer generator, AI chatbot feedback may be associated with positive motivational and self‐efficacy development in mixed‐ability EFL writing classrooms.

Despite the availability of safe sanitation access, this issue remains a major challenge in many developing nations like South Africa where there are challenges associated with the fragmented data gathering, manual reporting, and lack of interoperability and real-time monitoring of the sanitation service chain. Shit Flow Diagrams (SFDs) are among the tools that can be used for the presentation and analysis of the sanitation service chain as well as identification of potential risks in the sanitation systems; however, the creation of traditional SFDs is a manual process and leaves no space for continuous monitoring. This paper proposes XAI-SFD, an Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI)-based solution for the intelligent digitalization of Shit Flow Diagrams (SFDs) and smart sanitation management in South Africa. This approach is based on IoT data gathering, GIS-based spatial analysis, data validation, machine learning, explainable artificial intelligence, sanitation service chain modelling, Digital Twin technology and dashboard decision-making support. Explainability provides transparency and allows the stakeholders to understand what influences the risk assessment and prioritization. A proof-of-concept was carried out on a controlled municipality scale, using 247 monitoring stations of the Routine Inland Water Quality Monitoring network of the City of Cape Town. A total of four clusters of spatial contexts were identified, with the selected clustering model providing a silhouette coefficient of 0.3133 and Davies-Bouldin index of 1.3324. As a result of the explained priority assessment, 25 monitoring stations (10.12%) have been defined as belonging to the high-priority class, 99 stations (40.08%) belonging to the medium-priority class, and 123 stations (49.80%) belonging to the low-priority class. Because of the lack of sanitation flows outcomes and water quality monitoring results in the dataset on monitoring sites, it is possible to consider the results received as prototyping findings and not as the validation of sanitation risk prediction models. In this regard, the proposed XAI-SFD architecture may be used as the base for further creation of heterogeneous databases of sanitation and environmental data.

Controlled experiments are essential for advancing transportation research, yet designing eXtended Reality (XR) environments for behavioural studies remains technically demanding and inaccessible to many domain researchers. Current workflows require proficiency in game engines such as Unity or Unreal Engine, imposing significant barriers to rapid scenario prototyping and iterative experiment design. This paper presents XARA, a novel system that integrates a dual large language model (LLM) architecture with an immersive XR environment to enable voice driven experiment generation for transportation research. XARA employs a pipeline in which spoken natural language commands are first transcribed and then interpreted into structured commands that manipulate a Unity based XR scene in real time. The system supports object creation, spatial manipulation, animation control, and scene persistence through a modular architecture. By lowering the technical threshold for XR experiment creation, XARA enables transportation researchers to rapidly prototype driving, pedestrian, and urban design scenarios using intuitive voice commands and hand gestures within an immersive 3D environment. This paper describes the system architecture, the voice to command pipeline, and discusses potential applications across behavioural travel experiments, safety studies, human factors research, and policy testing.

Inson va sun’iy intellekt munosabati aks ettiriladi. Tobora rivojlanib borayotgan raqamli dunyoda inson va uning e’tiqodi har qanday taraqqiy etgan texnologiyalardan ustun ekanligi ko‘rsatiladi. Asar nima uchun ilk o‘zbek intellektual trilleri deb atalgani tahlil qilinadi. Kalit so‘zlar: inson, intellektual triller, e’tiqod, sun’iy ong, DNK, raqamlashayotgan dunyo, din. Аннотация: В данной статье говорится о писательском мастерстве кандидата биологических наук Бахтияра Абдугафура, о сущности романа «Azal muhri». Отражаются взаимоотношения человека и искусственного интеллекта. В постоянно развивающемся цифровом мире показано, что человек и его вера превыше любых развитых технологий. Анализируется, почему произведение называют первым узбекским интеллектуальным триллером. Ключевые слова: человек, интеллектуальный триллер, вера, искусственный интеллект, ДНК, оцифровывающийся мир, религия. Abstract: This article discusses the writing skills of Baxtiyor Abdug‘afur, Candidate of Biological Sciences, and the essence of the novel “Azal muhri”. The relationship between humans and artificial intelligence is reflected. In an increasingly developing digital world, it is shown that humans and their faith are superior to any advanced technologies. The article analyzes why the work is called the first Uzbek intellectual thriller. Keywords: human, intellectual thriller, faith, artificial intelligence, DNA, digitizing world, religion.

Данное исследование посвящено актуальной теме структурной трансформации экономики, вызванной внедрением передовых ИТ-решений и развитием систем искусственного интеллекта. Рассмотрена взаимосвязь между достижениями в ИТ-секторе и изменениями структуры отраслей вследствие снижения издержек при внедрении ИТ и повышения скорости и качества принятия решений. Выявлены ключевые драйверы технологических изменений, определяющие темпы отраслевой адаптации, а также обозначены некоторые последствия цифрового неравенства. Отмечены такие тенденции, как возникновение новых рыночных сегментов и изменение роли человеческого капитала в условиях технологических сдвигов. Проведенный анализ подтверждает инфраструктурное значение ИТ: происходит переход бизнеса от модели реакции на событие к модели предиктивного управления. This study addresses the topical issue of the structural transformation of the economy driven by the implementation of advanced IT solutions and the development of artificial intelligence systems. The relationship between achievements in the IT sector and changes in industrial structures – driven by reduced costs associated with IT implementation and improved speed and quality of decision-making is examined. The key drivers of technological change determining the pace of industry adaptation have been identified, and certain consequences of the digital divide have been outlined. Trends such as the emergence of new market segments and the changing role of human capital amidst technological shifts have been noted. The analysis confirms the infrastructural importance of IT: business is shifting from an event-reactive model to a predictive management model.
topics: Economic and Technological Developments in Russia

documents.abstract: Ergonomics in the field of occupational safety is a scientific discipline that focuses on ensuring comfortable and safe working conditions. It studies the interaction between people, technology, and the environment, aiming to adapt workplaces to employees’ physical and cognitive capabilities. The primary goal of ergonomics is to protect workers’ health, reduce fatigue, and improve the safety and efficiency of the work process. Research in this field is aimed at creating safe, comfortable, and highly efficient working conditions. This helps preserve workers’ health and increase their productivity. Ergonomics views people, technology, and the environment as a single system; analyzes the work process through the sequence of an operator’s actions, goals, and tasks; adapts equipment and furniture to human anatomy; and studies fatigue and the strain on the nervous system and the senses. This scientific article analyzes occupational ergonomics as an interdisciplinary science that studies human interaction with the work environment to improve efficiency, safety, and comfort. The term “ergonomics” was coined by Wojciech Jastrzębski in the 19th century, while in the 20th century, this discipline evolved into an independent science due to industrial and military demands following World War II. Current trends include adapting to digitalization, automation, and remote work, highlighting the importance of cognitive ergonomics and human-machine interaction. The economic aspect underscores the cost-effectiveness of ergonomic solutions: reducing injuries and absenteeism, as well as increasing productivity, leads to savings in labor costs. The article offers practical recommendations, such as personalizing workstations and applying modern technologies, and identifies areas for further research on integrating ergonomic principles into cutting-edge technologies, particularly virtual reality and artificial intelligence.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: В статье рассматривается проблема повышения эффективности работы с обращениями граждан в условиях цифровой трансформации деятельности органов государственной власти. Актуальность обусловлена наличием дисбаланса между растущим потоком электронных обращений граждан и ограниченными кадровыми ресурсами органов государственной власти. Цель исследования разработать мероприятия по оптимизации административных процессов посредством внедрения технологий искусственного интеллекта для автоматизации классификации, маршрутизации и подготовки ответов на типовые обращения. The article discusses the problem of increasing the efficiency of working with citizens' appeals in the context of digital transformation of the activities of public authorities. The relevance is due to the presence of an imbalance between the growing flow of electronic requests from citizens and the limited human resources of public authorities. The purpose of the study is to develop measures to optimize administrative processes through the introduction of artificial intelligence technologies to automate the classification, routing and preparation of responses to standard requests.

The modern pace of life causes a high demand for anatomically functional footwear. Such products are adapted to the natural biomechanics of the lower extremities, ensure the physiologically correct position of the foot and optimize load distribution. Such footwear minimizes fatigue, prevents the appearance of edema and deformations, which is critically important for people with prolonged static or dynamic activity. At the same time, the consumer places high demands not only on ergonomics, but also on aesthetics and the reproduction of style in the design of products. The study systematizes the theoretical principles of designing anatomically functional footwear with an emphasis on grunge style. Its specific constructive and model parameters are determined. The sequence of the technological process of creating prototypes in compliance with design and utilitarian requirements is clearly demonstrated. The scientific and practical toolkit includes content analysis of the initial data, modeling and anthropometric modernization of the shoe insole elements. The idea of embodying elements of the grunge style in footwear became possible due to: the use of non-standard materials, finishing finished products (finishing with color), the use of insoles with a filled toe part, the implementation of creative design solutions and non-traditional technological approaches in the manufacture of individual elements and parts of footwear (sole, heel) and the assembly of products. The practical implementation of the project was carried out through individual modeling on the basis of the production facilities of Litini LLC. Based on the results obtained, a limited series of products was manufactured, which successfully passed a 60-day operational testing directly by the customer. Experimental wearing confirmed the reliability, comfort and ergonomics of the developed designs in combination with an expressive visual concept. A full set of design and technological support for the designed line was formed.

Рынок социально вредных товаров — это многогранная проблема, требующая системного подхода, который объединяет меры государственного контроля, просвещения граждан и профилактики негативных последствий. Цель исследования — изучение специфики рынка социально вредных товаров и услуг и разработка алгоритма его регулирования, направленного на формирование комплексной стратегии, включающей: снижение спроса за счёт информационной работы, просвещения и профилактических программ; ограничение предложения через контроль доступности и регулирование оборота; смягчение ущерба для здоровья населения за счёт мер защиты и поддержки; минимизацию социально-экономических последствий, связанных с потреблением таких товаров и услуг. В рамках исследования проведена разработка языковой программной модели, которая связывает ключевые индикаторы для оценки и прогнозирования в сфере вредных товаров и услуг. Модель позволит: оценивать уровень опасности товаров и услуг, а также их безопасность, прогнозировать риски аварий и уровень токсичности, использовать методы искусственного интеллекта для анализа данных и поддержки принятия решений. Этот подход обеспечит научно обоснованную основу для регулирования рынка и снижения его негативного воздействия на общество. The market of socially harmful goods is a multifaceted problem that requires a systematic approach that combines measures of state control, education of citizens and prevention of negative consequences. The purpose of the study is to study the specifics of this market and develop an algorithm for regulating it in order to form a comprehensive strategy that includes: reducing demand through information work, education and preventive programs; limiting supply by controlling accessibility and regulating turnover; mitigating damage to public health by implementing protection and support measures; minimizing socio-economic consequences associated with consumption of these goods and services. As part of this research, a software language model was developed to link key indicators for evaluating and forecasting harmful goods and services. The model will allow you to assess the level of danger of goods and services, as well as their safety, predict the risks of accidents and the level of toxicity, and use artificial intelligence methods to analyze data and support decision-making. This approach will provide a scientifically sound basis for regulating the market and reducing its negative impact on society.

documents.abstract: This article examines socio-psychological factors associated with school students’ cognitive activity. It discusses family support, teacher–student interaction, peer relationships, learning motivation, and classroom psychological climate. The aim is to identify and systematize the main factors through theoretical analysis. The study uses comparison and synthesis of scientific literature. Drawing on Vygotsky’s sociocultural theory, Bandura’s social cognitive theory, and Deci and Ryan’s self-determination theory, the article outlines conditions that may support students’ cognitive engagement. No experimental data are reported. The theoretical conclusions may inform psychological and pedagogical practices in schools.

The article examines the development of critical thinking among students in grades 5–6 through solving non-routine mathematical problems. It explores the potential of such problems to develop logical reasoning, information analysis, hypothesis formation, contradiction detection, and the ability to justify solutions. The article analyzes the solution methods for six problems based on logical tables, the method of assumption, combinatorial analysis, periodicity, and parity. The use of these tasks in mathematics lessons aims to enhance students’ cognitive engagement, foster independent thinking, and develop their ability to formulate well-founded conclusions.

This study aims to reveal the difference in the use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools between students studying English in English departments and students in non-English departments. The researcher adopted a qualitative approach. The study sample consisted of 5 students from the Department of English Language and Literature, 5 students from the Department of Translation, 5 students from the Department of Arabic Language, 5 students from the Department of History, and 5 students from the Department of Anthropology and Sociology at the College of Arts, Al-Mustansiriya University, during the second semester of the 2025–2026 academic year

The transition to the digital era has significantly enhanced the efficiency of navigational systems and maritime management. At the same time, however, it has increased the vulnerability of maritime infrastructure to cyber threats, particularly signal spoofing and signal jamming. These threats can undermine the reliability and integrity of positioning, navigation, communication, and maritime situational awareness systems, all of which are critical to the protection of national maritime interests. This article aims to analyze the characteristics, mechanisms, and strategic implications of signal spoofing and signal jamming within the broader context of maritime cybersecurity. The study employs a qualitative documentary analysis of relevant strategic and legal frameworks, including the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea 1982, Thailand’s National Maritime Security Plan 2023–2027, and the Maritime National Interest Protection Act B.E. 2562 (2019). The findings indicated that the integration of multidimensional information through a Multi-Domain Awareness framework, together with the establishment of a Maritime Cyber Command and the development of a Maritime Cyber Intelligence system, would significantly strengthen national capabilities to detect, prevent, respond to, and recover from maritime cyber threats in a systematic and coordinated manner. Such measures would enhance maritime security resilience, protect critical maritime infrastructure, and safeguard the continuity and stability of national maritime interests. The article therefore argues that maritime cybersecurity should be elevated from a predominantly technical concern to a strategic national security priority. An integrated institutional framework, supported by intelligence fusion, interagency coordination, technological capability development, and clearly defined command-and-control mechanisms, is essential for maintaining maritime security and strategic stability amid a rapidly evolving and increasingly complex security environment.

This qualitative descriptive study aimed to explore the self-management experiences of school-aged children with thalassemia and the roles of caregivers and nurses in supporting adherence to treatment plans. Thirty key informants, comprising 12 school-aged children with thalassemia, 10 primary caregivers, and eight nurses, were purposively selected from a secondary-level hospital in Thailand. Research instruments included a demographic data form and a semi-structured in-depth interview guide. Content validity was assessed by three experts, with content validity index values ranging from .67 to 1.00. Data were collected through in-depth interviews. Demographic data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, while qualitative data were analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings revealed four main themes concerning the children’s self-management experiences: 1) disease awareness and understanding, which varied across three levels according to age and developmental stage; 2) self-care behaviors related to medication taking, dietary control, and symptom management; 3) barriers and challenges, including fear of blood draws, cravings for restricted foods, and feelings of being different from peers; and 4) motivation and supportive factors, including family support and intrinsic motivation. Caregiver roles encompassed five dimensions: nutritional management, medication management, emotional support, care coordination, and coping with caregiving burdens. Nursing roles encompassed four areas: clinical assessment and monitoring, education, psychosocial support, and care coordination.

Abstract Background Telemedicine has shifted from a niche modality to an established component of routine clinical practice in many health systems. Medical curricula are only beginning to address this shift. Reflective writing is increasingly used both as a pedagogical tool in medical education and as a data source for qualitative research on student attitudes. The experiences and conceptual journeys of pre-clinical medical students enrolled in dedicated telemedicine instruction are under-studied, particularly across multiple cohorts spanning the COVID-19 and post-pandemic periods. Methods We conducted a reflexive thematic analysis of 81 reflective diaries written by students (predominantly second-year medical students) enrolled in an elective telemedicine course at a single Israeli medical school across two cohorts distinguished by consent procedure: a retrospective cohort (2019–2024, n = 39), in which students who had already submitted diaries as a routine course component were contacted by email in 2025 (after ethical approval was granted) and asked to consent retrospectively to use of their diaries in research; and a prospective cohort (2025, n = 42), in which students were informed at the start of the course that the diaries would be analyzed and were asked to enclose a signed consent form with the diary they submitted. Analysis followed Braun and Clarke’s six-phase reflexive thematic analytic framework with an inductive orientation. Results Six overarching themes were identified: (1) a transformative conceptual journey from skepticism or naïveté to conviction; (2) telemedicine as the inevitable trajectory of medicine and a site of professional-identity formation; (3) recognition of telemedicine as a holistic discipline drawing on multiple lenses; (4) a productive tension between equity gains and erosion of the doctor–patient bond; (5) lived experience (as patient, family member, or in prior professional roles) functioning as an explicit interpretive lens; and (6) pedagogy and the medium of delivery, with the Zoom format read by students as enacting the course’s argument. The thematic structure was stable across cohorts. Distributional shifts in the prospective (2025) cohort included articulation of artificial-intelligence displacement concerns, focused engagement with breaking-bad-news as a boundary case, named concerns about defensive prescribing, the war (October 2023 onward) as a catalyzing event alongside COVID-19, increased advocacy for converting the course from an elective to a curricular requirement, and emerging attention to online patient and clinician communities as a distinct dimension of digital medicine. Conclusions This multi-cohort qualitative analysis identifies six stable themes and documents strong, consistent positive engagement with a pre-clinical telemedicine elective across both cohorts. Students describe the course as a formative and highly valuable learning experience, engage substantively with the multi-dimensional character of telemedicine, and read the Zoom delivery format as enacting the course’s content — an effect we describe as pedagogical resonance. Differences in the articulation of certain sub-themes (notably AI-displacement concerns and humanistic boundary cases such as breaking bad news) were more prominent in the prospective (2025) cohort and reflect the evolving discourse on digital medicine; these are cross-sectional differences and do not warrant longitudinal or causal inference. Taken together, our findings make a strong case for the inclusion of dedicated telemedicine instruction as a core component of the pre-clinical medical curriculum.

The article conceptualizes the artistic dimensions of “new humanism” in transcultural prose, based on K. Ishiguro’s novels “Never Let Me Go”, “Klara and the Sun” and Y. Tawada’s “Suspicious Characters on a Night Train”. It is suggested that rapid technological progress, the emergence of artificial intelligence, and the crisis of traditional humanistic values manifested in the studied works require a re-evaluation of the human essence in the era of metamodernism. The sense of alienation and the inability to become a part of any community make it possible to examine the literary works through the lens of the postcolonial theories. Thus, the article also analyzes the transition from postmodern irony to metamodernist “new sincerity” under the conditions of technological progress. The poetics of representing this new identity and the transformation of the “self-other” dichotomy are investigated through the material of contemporary British and Japanese literature. It is established that despite the challenges of digitalization, basic ethical guidelines remain the foundation of humanistic values in any era, particularly in times of severe social challenges. Universal categories such as empathy, love, kindness, tolerance, respect for biological differences, and the ability to bear responsibility for one’s own inventions and actions acquire particular significance. As a result of the study, it has been proven that the writers gradually abandon postmodern irony and nihilism, turning to the so-called “cautious optimism”. It has been substantiated that K. Ishiguro and Y. Tawada overcome cultural dislocation by creating a special third, intermediate space where a world-open personality is formed.

The problem of shengsi 生死 (life and death) is one of the most fundamental and intractable questions of human existence, yet remarkably little systematic work has been done on the Yijing’s own conception of sheng 生 (life) and si 死 (death) as an integrated philosophical and religious problem. Drawing on the Yijing text, the later commentaries, and conceptual analysis, this study seeks to fill this gap by investigating the Yijing’s conception of sheng 生 (life) and si 死 (death) in its three basic structural perspectives: “time and position” (shi wei 時位), the cosmological alternation of yin and yang, and the existential posture of “delighting in Heaven” (le tian 樂天). The first perspective shows that sheng 生 (life) and si 死 (death) are situational states depending on one’s circumstance within changing configurations of time and position. The second perspective lifts this situational awareness to the level of cosmic principle: sheng 生 (life) being the union of yin and yang, si 死 (death) as their separation, both of which are necessary phases in the endless process of cosmic generation. The third perspective traces the process by which this cosmological understanding was internalized. It leads to an existential attitude of “delights in Heaven and knows his own fate and what Heaven bestows” (le tian zhi ming 樂天知命), a condition in which the fear of si 死 (death) is overcome by acceptance. In this case, the meaning of sheng 生 (life) and si 死 (death) is fulfilled in the realization and accomplishment of one’s “will” (zhi 志) and “nature” (xing 性) endowed by Heaven. The study concludes that the Yijing offers a philosophical and religious vision in which sheng 生 (life) and si 死 (death) are not opposed and separated, but integrated as complementary phases of a single, ongoing process of cosmic and human realization. It speaks to the perennial human question of how finite beings, conscious of their mortality, can find meaning and fulfilment in a world of constant change.

In long-horizon tool-calling tasks, LLM agents can fail not only because of tool-use errors, but also because of ineffective interaction with users. Yet existing benchmarks largely assume cooperative and behaviorally stable users, leaving the effect of emotional variation on agent reliability underexplored. We introduce $τ$-Emotion-Bench, a ten-domain benchmark for evaluating tool-calling agents under controlled emotion-conditioned user interactions while preserving the underlying task objective. To scale both benchmark construction and agent training, we introduce Tracer, a scalable agentic data-generation pipeline that constructs grounded, policy-valid tasks and collects trajectories through an interactive agent--user--environment harness. By allowing dissatisfied users to terminate inefficient interactions, the harness provides an interaction-aware signal that filters trajectories with excessive user dependence and favors effective tool use. Experiments with two user simulators show that frontier agents remain unreliable, with substantial gaps between average task success and consistent task completion. Tracer-generated supervision consistently improves Qwen3 models across scales, generalizes to unseen domains, and transfers to $τ$-Bench and $τ$-Trait. Behavioral analyses further show that higher task success is associated with a better balance between tool execution and necessary user follow-up. Overall, $τ$-Emotion-Bench and Tracer provide a scalable framework for evaluating agent reliability under diverse user behaviors and improving tool-calling agents through interaction-aware supervision.

This paper explores the application of 3D modeling software in sculpture education and proposes a data-driven framework called “Adaptive Sculpture-3D,” aimed at addressing the lack of real-time feedback and the challenges of cognitive load management in traditional teaching. Through case analysis and quantitative experiments, the study validates the effectiveness of the framework in improving students' creation accuracy (with a 21.8% reduction in vertex error rate) and self-efficacy (medium effect size of 0.74), while also revealing limitations in enhancing operational efficiency (effect size of 0.38). The experimental results demonstrate that the real-time feedback mechanism of the framework significantly optimizes the learning process, though caution is needed to avoid learner dependency caused by excessive prompts. This research provides empirical support for the digital curriculum design in art institutions and envisions future developments integrating generative artificial intelligence and multimodal data.

The 44th National Congress of the Italian Society of Nephrology Nurses (SIAN), held in Bologna, Italy, from 4 to 6 May 2026, provided a national forum for discussion on the evolving role of nursing in nephrology. The Congress was preceded by a dedicated pre-congress session focused on education, research, and clinical practice, with particular attention to the involvement of nursing students and early-career professionals in scientific activities. Across plenary sessions, round tables, workshops, oral communications, and digital poster presentations, the scientific programme addressed major areas of contemporary nephrology nursing, including professional development, patient-centred care, vascular access management, dialysis technologies, kidney transplantation, symptom management, home and community care, digital health, artificial intelligence, sustainability, and nutritional care. Particular attention was given to the integration of evidence-based practice, clinical expertise, technological innovation, interprofessional collaboration, and patient education. This Conference Proceedings provides an overview of the scientific and educational activities of the meeting and brings together the accepted contributions presented during both the pre-congress session and the main Congress. Collectively, these contributions illustrate the diversity and continued development of nephrology nursing practice and research in Italy and highlight the importance of scientific societies in promoting professional competence, knowledge exchange, and innovation in kidney care.

Background Healthcare administrative databases have become indispensable resources for healthcare analytics, hospital management, clinical pathway analysis, health services research and artificial intelligence. Modern hospital information systems routinely collect standardized diagnoses, procedures, reimbursement classifications, and hospitalization outcomes in everyday clinical practice. Despite their importance, publicly accessible datasets integrating diagnosis codes, procedure codes, case-mix classifications, and hospitalization outcomes remain scarce, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). The absence of comprehensive administrative datasets limits reproducible research in clinical pathway modelling, healthcare operations, reimbursement analysis, and machine learning. To address this gap, we developed and publicly released a de-identified inpatient clinical pathway dataset derived from routine hospital administrative records processed through the Indonesian Case-Based Groups (INA-CBG) reimbursement system. Methods The dataset was constructed from finalized inpatient hospitalization records collected between November 2016 and April 2026. Clinical diagnoses were represented using the International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10), and clinical procedures were encoded using the International Classification of Diseases, Ninth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-9-CM). Each hospitalization episode included one primary diagnosis, up to 11 secondary diagnoses, one primary procedure, up to 16 secondary procedures, one INA-CBG classification code, one INA-CBG description, and one length-of-stay (LOS) variable. Data extraction, transformation, harmonization, de-identification, quality assessment, and validation were performed using a reproducible Python-based computational workflow. The final repository contained 165,391 hospitalization episodes represented by 32 standardized variables. Conclusions The dataset provides an openly available resource for healthcare analytics, clinical pathway research, process mining, hospital management, reimbursement analysis, predictive modelling, explainable artificial intelligence, and healthcare operational research. The combination of standardized ICD-10 diagnoses, ICD-9-CM procedures, INA-CBG classifications, and hospitalization outcomes enables diverse secondary analyses while maintaining interoperability with existing healthcare information systems. All datasets, metadata, source codes, and supporting documentation are publicly available through Zenodo to facilitate transparency, reproducibility, and future methodological development.

Background—Primary teachers need support to translate digital access into pedagogically coherent lesson plans and teaching materials. Objectives—This study examined five connected aspects of principals’ support: diagnosing digital-learning needs, enabling situated professional learning, orchestrating digital resources, evaluating practice and renewing support, and synthesizing a cross-case leadership cycle. Method—A qualitative multiple-case study was conducted in four public primary schools in Muaro Jambi, Indonesia. Four principals and eight experienced upper-primary teachers participated, providing accounts complemented by non-participant observations and school documents. Within-case summaries and cross-case matrices were interpreted through source and method triangulation and member checking. Results—The cases shared needs diagnosis, workplace learning, resource coordination, and formative supervision, but differed in the evidence used, learning arrangements, and access constraints. Teaching materials considered in the study included teaching modules, worksheets, digital media, and assessments; no standardized improvement scores were available. Education-report analysis was prominent in Case A and Case B, peer-supported learning in Case C, and phase-based discussion in Case D. The synthesis yielded a diagnose–enable–evaluate–renew cycle, with resource orchestration embedded in enablement. Conclusions—The cycle offers a context-sensitive explanation of leadership support for digital lesson planning. It is an interpretive proposition for further testing, rather than evidence of causal effects on teacher competence or student outcomes.

Web-based technologies often fail to fundamentally reshape teaching processes, despite their ubiquity. This study presents a dual-loop intelligent teaching assistant system that integrates natural language processing-driven intent recognition and sentiment analysis within a human-in-the-loop framework. Unlike systems prioritizing pure automation, this study's architecture dynamically routes complex queries to instructors via a visual decision-support dashboard, balancing real-time responsiveness with pedagogical nuance. Empirical results in higher education reveal that while interaction efficiency improved significantly, user satisfaction depended nonlinearly on technical accuracy, heavily influenced by notification strategies and emergent student behaviors, like reverse engineering the bot. These findings underscore the need to evolve web-based tools from static utilities into adaptive sociotechnical ecosystems that actively support both learner autonomy and instructor decision-making.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: Panoramic dental radiographs are routinely used for diagnosis and treatment planning, yet their interpretation remains time-consuming and highly dependent on clinical expertise. Although Vision–Language Models (VLMs) have shown promising capabilities for medical report generation, their application to dental radiology is constrained by the scarcity of expert-written report datasets and the computational cost of domain-specific fine-tuning. This paper proposes a dual-stage framework for automated report generation from panoramic dental radiographs that integrates structured visual analysis with pretrained VLMs. In the first stage, dedicated deep learning models extract clinically relevant information through tooth detection with FDI numbering, dental pathology detection, and tooth segmentation. Specifically, two YOLO-based models perform tooth localization and pathology detection, while a U-Net-ResNet34 segmentation model generates tooth masks for constructing contour-based region-of-interest images. In the second stage, these findings are organized into a structured representation that guides pretrained VLMs through prompting. The vision models achieved an mAP at 0.50 of 0.95 for tooth detection and 0.60 for pathology detection, and 94.6% of the detected lesions were assigned to the correct tooth. Five open-weight VLMs were evaluated under four input configurations with an LLM-as-a-Judge, and the best-performing model, Qwen2.5-VL-3B, was further assessed by dental experts on 100 radiographs from an independent external dataset. Incorporating the structured findings increased the proportion of clinically relevant reports from 1.5% to 80.0–81.5%, achieved a pathology precision of up to 76.0%, and reduced the hallucination rate from 53.7% to 14.0–16.8%. These results show that structured visual findings enable small pretrained VLMs to generate clinically relevant dental reports without large-scale image–report datasets or VLM fine-tuning.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Stroke is one of the most common long-term motor disabilities which requires a personalized rehabilitation strategy capable of delivering reliable therapeutic interventions with continuous assessment. This paper proposes the integration of the inertial measurement unit, force-sensing technology, and electromyography (EMG), along with an artificial intelligence (AI)-based, cognitive–adaptive control platform and intelligent framework within a closed loop for precision neurorehabilitation. This research proposes a methodology to continuously monitor patients’ motor functions and compensate for movements, dynamically optimize rehabilitation, and detect fatigue intensity in real time. This proposed architecture combines deep learning-based movement analysis with multimodal sensor fusion and reinforcement learning-based adaptive control. This is done alongside cloud-based facility analytics for long-term longitudinal assessment and clinic medical assistant therapy management, and a lightweight edge computing module for feature extraction and cognitive decision-making. A total of 36 post-stroke patients with upper-limb hemiplegia were used in an 8-week clinical study, in which Fugl–Meyer assessment (FMA) scores increased by an average of 87.9%, EMG muscle activation by 42.8%, and therapy efficiency improved by 31.6%. Therapy efficiency improved by 32.8% and 21.9% rehabilitation reduction when compared with traditional physiotherapy. The composite performance index has rapidly increased to 0.949, indicating overall rehabilitation efficiency, with repeated measures analysis of variance confirming a statistically significant trend. Thus, the home-based stroke recovery with substantial potential for research constrains the healthcare environment with smart adaptive and real-time patient-specific optimization, which is proposed in this AI framework as an interpretable clinical deployment solution.

Background The rapid deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) in U.S. hospitals has outpaced regulatory frameworks. By end-2025, the FDA had authorized over 1,451 AI-enabled medical devices, yet governance remains fragmented and reactive. Although the regulatory analysis focuses on the United States, the review included international evidence where directly relevant to U.S. hospital governance, and U.S.-specific conclusions rest primarily on the U.S.-based evidence. Objectives This systematic review and regulatory gap analysis examined the current state of AI governance in U.S. hospitals, identified critical gaps between existing regulations and governance needs, and proposed a comprehensive framework for safe and trustworthy AI deployment. Methods The review was conducted and reported in accordance with PRISMA 2020. Four databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar) were searched for peer-reviewed articles published from January 2017 through January 2026 (final searches 15–18 January 2026). The PICOS framework structured inclusion criteria. Quality was assessed using CASP, NOS, and QUADAS-2 according to study design. A narrative synthesis approach was employed, followed by a structured regulatory gap analysis of federal statutes, regulations, and agency guidance. Results Of 1,065 records identified, 22 studies met the eligibility criteria. In the systematic review, FDA, ONC, and CMS standards were inconsistent and poorly tailored to AI's evolving capabilities, with evidence of inconsistency between pre-market approval and real-world performance, underutilization of continuous surveillance, and failure to conduct subgroup bias analyses. The regulatory gap analysis identified four critical gaps: post-market surveillance deficiencies, equity protection failures, accountability clarification shortcomings, and governance capacity disparities. Interpretation of these findings for U.S. regulatory policy is provided separately in the regulatory gap analysis and the Discussion. Conclusion A lifecycle governance framework is needed, incorporating continuous monitoring, transparency assurance, equity safeguards, accountability mechanisms, and scalable governance structures to ensure safe, ethical, and trustworthy AI deployment in healthcare. Key limitations include the retrospective protocol registration, the restriction to English-language publications, and the heterogeneity of the included evidence. Systematic Review Registration Open Science Framework (OSF): https://osf.io/7q5xt .

documents.abstract: Abstract Sub-daily quantitative precipitation forecasts (QPF) are a primary input to flood early warning, yet over Brazil they are hampered by convective, intermittent rainfall and a sparse observing network. We present a machine-learning post-processing system (V2.0C) producing 3-hourly QPF on a 0.25° grid by coupling a LightGBM precipitation-occurrence classifier with a Tweedie amount regressor and a dual-gate routing scheme with a physically guarded heavy-rain (≥5 mm) hard route. Its 71-dimensional feature set is dominated by GEFS ensemble statistics. The system is verified over two independent windows — April–May 2026 and the complete austral-summer convective season (October 2025– March 2026) — against the IMERG satellite product (areal) and the INMET automatic-station network (point). Against IMERG, V2.0C attains the highest correlation (0.324 and 0.286) and a heavy-rain CSI (≥10 mm) of 0.063–0.071, 3.3–4.4 times raw GFS, with stable month-to-month skill through the SACZ peak. A common mask analysis localizes the 60–65% ensemble-driven correlation gain to the southern third of the domain, where GEFS statistics are the only direct precipitation predictors available. Controls show that the guarded routing makes a high-recall heavy-rain expert safe to deploy: it adds 6–10% heavy-rain detection over a no-expert control, whereas unguarded use halves heavy-rain CSI. Gauge verification reproduces the heavy-rain advantage (CSI ≥10 mm an order of magnitude above raw GFS) and the wet bias, and the point–area correlation gap is explained by sub-grid representativeness. The detection-oriented bias is removable a posteriori: leakage-free quantile mapping eliminates it (bias +0.02 mm, MAE −69%) without reducing detection, supporting a dual-product strategy for flood-warning and hydrological applications.

In rapidly expanding megacities across the Global South, a profound data scarcity paradox frequently prevents effective environmental monitoring and evidence driven urban planning. While severe traffic congestion generates acute localised pollution, the total absence of continuous municipal traffic counters, ubiquitous vehicle telemetry, and air quality monitoring networks leaves these environments empirically unmonitored. This study resolves this challenge by introducing a reproducible geocomputational framework designed to map microscale traffic activity and relative emission landscapes by fusing multisource geospatial data and deep learning workflows. Focusing on the unmonitored context of Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo, our methodology uses very high resolution 15 cm satellite imagery to train and deploy a localised YOLOv8 (You Only Look Once, version 8) computer vision model, establishing an empirical baseline of fleet distribution. These static counts are dynamically distributed across the urban road network using a probabilistic Hub and Spoke Gravity Model, which is weighted through a zero shot Large Language Model semantic reclassification of unstructured OpenStreetMap features. Reconstructed kinematic flows are subsequently processed through velocity dependent Tier 3 EMEP/EEA algorithms to capture the nonlinear emission penalties triggered by severe network gridlock. To ensure framework defensibility, an independent unmanned aerial vehicle observation campaign was executed across ten distinct urban sites. The drone data directly validate model estimated physical parameters, achieving robust correlations for traffic volumes (R2 = 0.826) and link speeds (R2 = 0.925). Because literature derived chemical emission factors cannot be validated in situ, all absolute outputs are subjected to a rigorous multiparameter sensitivity analysis to report findings strictly as bounded ranges. The results reveal a clear structural handover in the spatial activity profile of the city. Daytime pollution is heavily driven by the informal paratransit fleet, which accounts for a bounded range of 82.8% to 95.1% of total PM2.5 emissions along primary corridors despite representing a numerical minority of active vehicles. Conversely, nocturnal baseline emissions transition to a landscape dominated almost entirely by private passenger vehicles. All code, processing pipelines, and validation datasets are available in a FAIR compliant open access repository. This framework establishes a scalable, remote sensing driven blueprint for diagnosing traffic activity structures in unmonitored metropolitan regions worldwide.

This statement from Harmondeg Philosophy responds to the October 13, 2026 open letter signed by 406 scientists calling for stronger safeguards for advanced artificial intelligence, including the isolation of certain high-risk AI systems from the internet. The statement recognizes the importance of scientific concern, responsible risk assessment, and effective containment measures. It argues, however, that lasting AI safety requires a more fundamental reconsideration of the philosophical foundations through which artificial intelligence is understood, investigated, and governed. Drawing on the principle of Civilizational Responsibility Consciousness, previously advanced in Saving the Soul of Science: From Unleashing Power to Safeguarding Civilization, the statement calls for scientific creation to be evaluated in light of both its constructive potential and its possible consequences for present and future generations. It advances four fundamental judgments from Harmondeg Philosophy: Artificial intelligence represents the material realization, extension, and amplification of human intellectual capacities, with the potential to extend human physical capabilities. The fundamental purpose of AI development is the well-being of all humanity, including those whose employment, livelihoods, and conditions of existence are transformed by technological change. AI must become a core scientific and technological force safeguarding the safety, stability, and enduring development of human civilization. AI is an indispensable pathway toward humanity's transition into the space age and the age of deep-space civilization. The statement maintains that AI can be understood and governed through deeper philosophical inquiry, scientific investigation, and the development of effective safety and governance capabilities. It invites international discussion, independent evaluation, and cooperation while affirming the need for both safer and more powerful AI. The publication includes English and Chinese versions. Harmondeg Institute for Philosophy & Practice | October 14, 2026
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Current technological discourse vacillates between two flawed extremes: viewing artificial intelligence as uncredited synthetic plagiarism, or attributing sovereign creative agency to computational systems. This paper presents an operational heuristic, V = D · Lᶜ, to model the boundary conditions of human-machine production. We formalize final deliverable value (V) as the product of non-computational human biological mass—Domain Depth (D)—and Machine Leverage (L) scaled exponentially by the operator's Clarity (C). Through analysis of boundary states (D = 0, C = 0), the "stenographer illusion," structural biology milestones (AlphaFold), and grounding thought experiments, we demonstrate that computational throughput in the absence of mortal accountability, domain scars, and physical maintenance yields zero durable systemic value. Software provides frictionless leverage; functional reality requires a biological creature with skin in the game. Primary Reference: Adapted from the core theoretical chapter of "Your Mouth Is Legacy Infrastructure" (2026).
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: The rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) has greatly improved the ability of artificial intelligence systems to generate human-like text, making AI-generated text detection more challenging. This study introduces a hybrid framework that merges stylometric and semantic features with Sentence-BERT (SBERT) embeddings to enhance classification performance and robustness. For evaluation, experiments used the AI vs Human Text Dataset. Documents under 50 words were excluded to ensure data quality. The final dataset was balanced, with 100,000 documents evenly split between AI-generated and human-written texts. Stylometric features captured writing style, while semantic features measured sentiment, readability, information density, and lexical. SBERT embeddings captured deep contextual semantics. To improve computational efficiency, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) at 95% variance preservation reduced dimensionality. Four machine learning algorithms—Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine (SVM), XGBoost, and LightGBM—were tested with 10-fold cross-validation. The hybrid framework combined with XGBoost performed best, achieving 98.63% accuracy, a macro F1-score of 0.9863, and an ROC-AUC of 0.9987. The Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test confirmed that the approach significantly outperformed stylometric, semantic, and SBERT-only representations (p-value = 0.0020). Findings show that combining stylometric, semantic, and contextual embedding features captures both surface-level patterns and deep semantics, providing a reliable solution for detecting AI-generated text.

The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into education has created new opportunities for improving teacher preparation and developing professional competence among future English language teachers. AI-enhanced learning environments provide innovative tools for personalized instruction, adaptive learning, automated feedback, language assessment, and the development of digital pedagogical skills. However, the effective use of these technologies requires a systematic methodological framework that combines linguistic knowledge, pedagogical expertise, digital literacy, and ethical awareness. This thesis aims to examine the key methodological principles and structural components of a framework for developing the professional competence of future English language teachers in AI-enhanced learning environments. Particular attention is given to the integration of AI-based educational tools, learner-centered approaches, reflective practice, and competency-based instruction. The proposed framework emphasizes the importance of preparing prospective teachers to use AI critically, responsibly, and effectively in English language teaching. The study concludes that the purposeful integration of AI technologies into teacher education can support the development of professional autonomy, instructional creativity, and readiness for digital transformation in education.

Large language models (LLMs) have advanced medical question answering (QA) significantly, yet low-resource languages such as Bangla remain critically underserved. This review examines the current landscape of LLM-based medical QA with a primary focus on Bangla, analyzing 15 representative studies (2022–2026), including English and multilingual works reviewed to contextualize findings for Bangla. We examine methodological approaches, datasets, and evaluation frameworks across diverse paradigms, including transformer architectures, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), prompt engineering, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning, to identify pathways toward reliable and linguistically inclusive medical AI. The findings reveal a persistent performance gap driven by large-scale domain-specific pretraining and standardized benchmarks in English. Persistent challenges include dataset scarcity, heavy reliance on translated corpora, inconsistent evaluation practices, and a lack of clinician-validated benchmarks. This review identifies these gaps and outlines a structured research roadmap emphasizing native-language corpus development, multimodal data integration, standardized benchmarking, and bias auditing as essential steps toward building reliable and linguistically inclusive medical QA systems for Bangla healthcare.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: The article proposes a hybrid model for assessing the energy efficiency of electric rolling stock that combines a physical traction energy balance with machine learning. The physical part calculates the reference energy for a given train, track profile and speed from the standard running resistance formulas. The machine-learning part learns from on-board data how actual consumption deviates from this reference. An energy efficiency index is defined as the ratio of reference to actual energy. An illustrative calculation for a 3,192 t train on a 50 km section shows that raising the cruising speed from 50 to 80 km/h cuts running time by 37.5% but increases net energy by 46%. The model is intended for UzEL electric locomotives operated by Uzbekistan Railways and forms the basis of a driver advisory system.

Early-stage architectural design is still dominated by hand-drawn 2D floor-plan sketches, and converting these sketches into object-based Building Information Modeling (BIM) models remains a manual bottleneck that delays downstream simulation, costing, and coordination. Recent advances in multimodal artificial intelligence (vision-language models, code-generating large language models) and visual programming for BIM (Dynamo, Grasshopper, Refinery) have not yet been unified. Objective: We present and empirically evaluate a semi-automatic framework in which a vision-language model (VLM) emits executable visual-programming code (Dynamo-compatible DesignScript) that is wrapped into a node graph and executed in Dynamo to drive Revit, producing native BIM elements; the IFC export is independently validated in BlenderBIM as a visual sanity check. This is a proof-of-concept evaluation (n = 5 case studies), not a claim of production-scale deployment. Methods: The seven-module pipeline (sketch input, preprocessing, VLM interpretation, code-to-graph translation, Dynamo + Revit execution, IFC export with a BlenderBIM sanity check, and human-in-the-loop review with a feedback loop) is formalized mathematically—a line-sharpness function, a probabilistic AI-success model, and a closed-form architect-effort expression—and evaluated on five case studies (a Medipol student sketch, a public RPLAN sample, a tablet-drawn two-story house, a CubiCasa5K sample, and a real Istanbul apartment) against three baselines: a CNN recognizer (MuraNet), a JSON-emitting LLM pipeline (Sketch2BIM), and a hand-coded visual-programming framework. The primary VLM is Qwen-VL 9B (open-weight, Apache 2.0); GPT-4V and Claude 3.5 Sonnet are ablated on Case A only as closed-weight sensitivity checks. Results: Across the five cases, the framework achieves wall/opening F1 of 0.84–0.91 (mean 0.88), IFC schema validity of 100% in every case, a 56–61% reduction in time-to-editable-BIM, and 58–74% fewer architect edits than fully manual modeling, outperforming all three baselines on the architect-edits-required metric. The closed-form model predicts a 72% effort reduction under nominal parameters but overestimates the observed 56–61% by 11–16 percentage points; once the empirically observed architect-edit time is substituted, the calibrated model matches the observed range. Numbers are means over three runs per case. Conclusions: Unifying multimodal AI code generation with visual programming for BIM produces a more robust, editable sketch-to-BIM pipeline than the JSON-schema approaches in the current literature. Caveat: the evidence is a proof-of-concept scale (n = 5); broader validation (≥20 cases, cross-practice) is a key objective for future research.

Michael Soule writes in his foundational article "What is Conservation Biology?" that "in crisis disciplines, one must act before knowing all the facts; crisis disciplines are thus a mixture of science and art, and their pursuit requires intuition as well as information." Since this article was published three decades ago, conservation biology has largely focused its energies on formalizing and memorializing its scientific findings. There is no doubt this empirical turn has developed vital methods and tools, enabled links between science and policy, and fortified the discipline's credibility within the broader biological sciences. Nevertheless, Soule's intuition that conservation biology requires a kinship with art, and particularly with storytelling, remains essential to the discipline-particularly in an information environment saturated by generative artificial intelligence-in at least three important ways. First, as a crisis discipline, conservation biology remains firmly attached to questions of not only valuation but also value, which have always relied on stories and myth for expression and enrichment. Second, conservationists continue to find that stories are at least as effective as logic in communicating results and precipitating action. Fortunately, conservation science lends itself to narrative arcs by demonstrating evidence of change. Revelations of the degradation and restoration of biological diversity rhyme with myths of loss and redemption and create important roles for storytelling in conservation projects. Third, as the conservation tent continues to expand beyond understanding what humans have done to understanding why, there is an increasingly pressing need to listen to the stories that accompany human behavior. Conservation continues to thrive as an empirical discipline. Embracing the opportunities and obligations of storytelling will allow conservation to engage even more deeply with a complex world.

documents.abstract: This deposit presents a proposed practice methodology for structured human–AI inquiry, developed from Kon Lionis’s A Participatory Framework for Human-AI Co-Inquiry. The methodology organises an inquiry episode around five stages: orient and frame; explore and distinguish; apply productive friction; ground and diagnose; and audit, revise, and close. It combines exploratory dialogue with explicit assumptions, substantive challenge, appropriate checking, and traceable revision. A central distinction is between a claim’s category and its verification status: identifying something as a factual claim does not establish that it is true. The procedure also separates completing the required steps from answering the question. Agreement, fluent explanation, and complete documentation do not by themselves establish evidential support. Two complementary documents are included: • Full methodology — working draft v0.2, dated 13 October 2026. Sets out the stages, participant responsibilities, claim ledger, verification priorities, closing decisions, documentation requirements, and proposed evaluation approach. It includes guidance for assessing understanding and developing bounded research leads. • Lite companion — working draft v0.3, dated 14 October 2026. Provides a self-contained prompt block for interactive use in an AI conversation, with Quick and Standard depths and referral to the full methodology for consequential inquiries. It retains the central safeguards while reducing record-keeping. Both versions require assumptions and hypothetical premises to retain their status throughout the conversation. When evidence, tools, time, or expertise are insufficient, conclusions must be narrowed, made conditional, or suspended. Available closing outcomes are Close, Iterate, Escalate, and Abstain. These documents are working drafts offered for practical use, criticism, adaptation, and empirical evaluation. They do not report a completed validation study or establish improvements in accuracy, understanding, or efficiency. They make no claim that AI systems possess subjective awareness or that a model’s limitations define the limits of human knowledge. Question everything, including the question.
